alignments.note: Participle rendered with subject pronoun and auxiliary; head on the lexical predicate (rules 17, 24).
Nomen rectum; the ASV writes with rather than of for the relation (rule 19).

The ASV supplies and to coordinate two asyndetic Hebrew participial phrases. Counting coordination markers by the pair of elements each joins (rule 42's reasoning), the waw at s004 joins the right-hand and left-hand terms and the waw at s009 joins the two in- phrases, so no morpheme licenses this and (rule 30).

Hiphil participle rendered could use the right hand; head on right by rule 31's subtraction, since use alone uses anything. The correlative both at t009 is placed with the waw it pairs with rather than absorbed here.

The waw stands between the right-hand and left-hand terms, and the ASV realizes that coordination by the correlative pair both ... and; the unit is discontinuous under rule 25 and headed on the and, which carries the conjunction proper. Competing reading keeps both inside the preceding participle's unit, but both is written for the coordination the waw supplies and nothing else licenses it (rule 30).
Second participle rendered the left, with a supplied the, no article morpheme being present (rule 29).
Preposition rendered in.
The ASV writes in slinging stones with no the (rules 12, 29).

review_notes: Three English ands against two waws: t013 and t019 are placed by rule 42's test of which elements the and joins, leaving t006 added.

Correction: the correlative both at t009 moves from the s003 unit to the s004 waw unit. both ... and is one coordinating construction realizing the waw, so the unit is discontinuous under rule 25; nothing but the coordination licenses both, and rule 30 forbids reaching for added where a morpheme licenses the English.
